transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-11
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Arclight CTO), Ravi Singh (Arclight Head of Cloud), Priya Malhotra (Arclight SecOps)

Summary: High-level discovery for private deployment of Redwood inference behind Arclight VPC. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; leaning Private for data residency and compliance. Focus: networking model, peering, private endpoints, region availability, KMS access, and pilot requirements.

00:00 Lena: okay thanks everyone for joining, um yeah we sent over the calendar, this is lena ortiz from arclight, CTO. we wanted to run through the network and security side for running inference  on our side, private vpc deployment.
00:12 Maya: awesome, thanks Lena. i'm maya chen, AE at Redwood, joining with devon our solutions engineer. quick agenda: understand your infra + constraints, discuss peering versus endpoints, talk kms/hsm access, and agree next steps for a pilot. does that work?
00:28 Ravi: yep that sounds good. i've got a couple of network folks standing by if we need deeper details.
00:30 Devon: quick intro on our side: Redwood Private can run in your VPC via VPC peering or customer-managed private endpoints. there are a few flavors - direct peering, transit gateway, or interface endpoints depending on your cloud architecture. usually recommend peering for low-latency inference traffic but open to details.
00:52 Priya: can you clarify difference between peering and endpoints? we want to avoid public egress for any inference requests.
01:05 Devon: sure. VPC peering establishes a direct route between our dedicated workload VPC and your VPC - traffic stays inside the cloud backbone, no public ip. Private endpoints (like AWS Interface endpoints / PrivateLink) expose a service endpoint in your VPC and you'll do interface ENIs -> also private. peering gives full routing, endpoints are per-service and are sometimes easier for multi-account setups. peering also means you need non-overlapping CIDRs.
01:34 Lena: non-overlapping CIDRs is concerning - we've got several legacy VPCs with /16s. how strict is that?
01:42 Devon: you need unique ranges to peer. if overlaps, options are transit gateway + NAT or using PrivateLink. there are tradeoffs - Transit GW can route across regions but cost/logistics differ. also mention that some clouds don't allow cross-region peering so you'd use replication or regional endpoints.
02:05 Ravi: we run most workloads in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for redundancy; question is do you support cross-region private deployments or do we need separate peering per region?
02:15 Maya: good question. Redwood Private runs in-region - we deploy the inference cluster in the region you specify. for cross-region redundancy you'd normally set up a sibling cluster in the other region and peer each cluster to the local VPC. we do not do transparent cross-region single-PEM by default.
02:35 Priya: uptime SLA? if we have two regional clusters how do failover and routing work?
02:42 Devon: you can set routing policy at the app layer - route to local region, failover to other region via DNS or application fallback. Redwood Console supports per-route model and fallback policies, but routing across regions is handled by your networking or the app.
03:03 Lena: what about egress IPs? our partner integrations require allowlisting static outbound IPs for webhooks. can you provide stable egress IPs from the Redwood side?
03:13 Devon: we can provide egress IP ranges when you're on Dedicated/Private. If you peer into our VPC, outbound requests from the inference runtime will originate from our managed NAT or an egress subnet - we can publish the IPs for allowlisting. if you host fully in your VPC (private package on-prem or bring-your-own infra) it's your IPs.
03:34 Ravi: fine, we need a list for compliance. also want to understand NAT vs IGW vs PrivateLink for egress.
03:41 Devon: typically traffic to external APIs goes via NAT in our managed subnet. for strict controls you can set up VPC endpoints for S3 or other services to avoid public egress. for webhook allowlisting, static egress IPs are simplest.
04:05 Priya: encryption at rest and KMS: can we bring our own keys? we require keys that we control for model data and logs.
04:12 Maya: yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments. you can supply KMS keys and we integrate with customer-managed KMS. for HSM we have partners/integration patterns - we should capture your exact requirements.
04:30 Lena: what about access to the KV cache and model artifacts - do those live in your managed S3 bucket or in our bucket?
04:39 Devon: model artifacts can be stored in a customer bucket if you want full control. KV cache is runtime-managed but can be configured to persist to a customer-managed store. there are a couple of deployment patterns in our runbook. we'll share the runbook and config examples.
04:58 Ravi: latency numbers - what should we expect for token latency when peered in us-east-1?
05:05 Devon: with in-region peering, typical p95 token latency from request to first token is in the low hundreds of milliseconds for small models and around 200-400ms for the medium sizes - depends on batch size, model, sequence length. we'll give perf profiles.
05:26 Lena: we're considering two workloads: synchronous chat for operators (latency sensitive), and batch embeddings for analytics (throughput sensitive). recommended setup?
05:36 Devon: run chat on a low-latency pool (smaller batch sizes, reserved capacity). embeddings can use higher batching across larger instances to save cost. Redwood Optimize will also recommend quantization/profile for cost.
05:55 Priya: compliance: SOC2, ISO, audit logs - do you produce access/audit logs for the private control plane?
06:03 Maya: yes, we provide audit logs, per-token cost traces, and can integrate with your SIEM via Kinesis or Splunk forwarders. SOC2 Type II and ISO are in our pack - we'll attach the security whitepaper.
06:20 Ravi: network peering specifics: we are hybrid multi-account. ideally we want to avoid opening peering with every account. can we use Transit Gateway?
06:29 Devon: transit gateway is a good pattern - you peer the Redwood cluster VPC to your transit gateway, and then attach accounts. it supports multi-account, and can help avoid a web of pairings. downside: extra cost and you need region-available TGW. we'll include a sample TGW diagram.
06:50 Priya: any gotchas with PrivateLink and DNS? we've had issues with split-horizon and internal routing before.
06:58 Devon: yes DNS resolution is important - with interface endpoints you'll typically create private hosted zones or endpoint-specific DNS entries. split-horizon can cause surprises if you have internal names overlapping. we'll show the recommended DNS records and validation steps.
07:22 Lena: timeline - we want a 2-week pilot to validate latency and egress controls. is that feasible?
07:29 Maya: yes, typically pilot can be 1-3 weeks. steps: we send runbook + pricing, you provide AWS account IDs + CIDRs, we set up peering or endpoints, run smoke tests and perf benchmarks.
07:45 Ravi: action: we can share account IDs and CIDRs by friday (8/13).
07:50 Priya: i'll compile compliance Qs and send them too.
07:56 Maya: perfect. i'll send SOC2, network runbook, and a draft topology diagram by tomorrow. devon will prepare the TGW/peering options diagram.
08:05 Devon: one more note - if you require HSM-backed keys for inference decryption at runtime, we'll need to discuss latency implications; HSM calls can add 10s-100s ms depending on pattern. there's a hybrid approach: use HSM for key wrapping and KMS for day-to-day operations.
08:27 Lena: good to know, we'll flag that with the security team.
08:35 Priya: can we get a list of required IAM roles/policies for the peering + s3 access? we prefer least privilege upfront.
08:44 Devon: yes we'll include an example IAM policy for model artifact access, KMS decrypt, and peering setup. also include sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets.
09:02 Maya: recap on next steps: Redwood to send runbook, security whitepaper, pricing for Dedicated+Private, and network diagrams. Arclight to send account IDs/CIDRs and compliance Qs. schedule 60-min technical deep dive wk of 8/16.
09:20 Lena: okay thanks, that covers it from our side.
09:25 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and proposed times.
09:32 call ends

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings present (eg 'K-V cash' for KV cache in one auto-snippet), occasional speaker label drift, filler words left in. referenced artifacts: link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-vpc (shared after call), pricing sheet (link to drive), sample TGW diagram (attached).
